conclusions: Both independent work reductions and their combination beat vc16 in core API, full API and repeated CUPTI medians.
The combined candidate is fastest: full API 25.6150 ms versus vc16 27.1694 and original Sage 26.5558 ms.
Combined candidate beats vc16 and original Sage in each of the three CUPTI trial medians. Raw API trials are unavailable, so no confidence interval or general speed guarantee is inferred.

All reported candidates have the same 168 registers, zero local bytes, 41088 shared bytes and predicted three resident blocks. This gain comes from the changed instruction paths/scheduling, not an increase in predicted occupancy.
Integer max alone saves 1.1052 ms full API versus vc16; identity-scaling skip alone saves 0.6067 ms; together save 1.5544 ms. Independent effects are not additive.
Initial stage tables and one-off traces measure unchanged default vc15, not the work-reduction candidates.
Use vc22_both as the next experimental baseline. Public default remains vc15; the measured winner requires explicit kernel_mode selection with v_smooth=False.
This is Sage INT8 QK plus ExpCast without V smoothing, not a validation of the complete VC paper or its end-to-end model speedup.
